newsitem.title: UK: Major warns of "overmighty" unions under Labour.
newsitem.headline: Major warns of "overmighty" unions under Labour.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Tuesday the election of a Labour government could lead to the re-emergence of "overmighty" trade unions that could threaten Britain's industrial prosperity.

Major was speaking during a campaign trip to the Midlands, whose motor industry, he said, had been transformed from a basket case in the 1970s to a success story in the 1990s thanks to Conservative trade union reforms and tax cuts.

Major told reporters that the main opposition Labour party's plans to require firms to recognise trade unions where more than half the workforce chose to be represented by them "put potentially at risk many of the improvements that we have seen".

"To try and turn back those trade union reforms and go back to the sort of circumstances where you had overmighty trade unions damaging both companies' and employees' rights would be one of the most retrograde steps you could possibly see."

Major also attacked Labour leader Tony Blair for his support of the European Union's Social Chapter on workplace rights, saying this would open the door to the sort of policies that had sent unemployment soaring in continental Europe.

Major challenged Blair to explain why he would not legislate in Britain for the same policies that would be introduced through the Social Chapter. The reason, Major said, is that parliament would simply not approve them.
"When we have unemployment falling and falling rapidly, it seems to me folly in the extreme to reintroduce the policies that across Europe are putting unemployment up," Major said.
